STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of mashed potato and roasted/fried potato chunks (or similar starchy cubes) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle, on a glass table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate roughly 26 cm across (dinner plate). Vessel area ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.8 (rounded corners) ≈ 540 cm^2; using a circular equivalent of 26 cm diameter gives 530 cm^2. Use ~530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Mashed potato (white, with black pepper flecks)
- Roasted/fried potato cubes (golden, crispy edges)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Mashed potato covers roughly 40% of the plate (~210 cm^2), piled up to ~2.5 cm.
- Roasted potato pieces cover roughly 20% (~105 cm^2), about 2 cm thick.
- Total food coverage ≈ 60% of the plate, which is consistent with what is visible.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Mashed potato: 210 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 525 ml
- Roasted potato: 105 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 210 ml (about 8 cubes of roughly 3 cm each, consistent with the visible pieces)

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Mashed potato: 525 ml x 0.9 ≈ 470 g
- Roasted potato: 210 ml x 0.7 (cut/cubed, with air gaps) ≈ 150 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Mashed potato, ~100 kcal/100 g (made with some butter/milk): 470 g → ~470 kcal
- Roasted potato, ~150 kcal/100 g (oil-fried/roasted): 150 g → ~225 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 620 g of food on a dinner plate with roughly 60% coverage is plausible for a generous main-course portion of mashed and roasted potato. Mashed potato at 0.9 g/ml may be a slight overestimate given the loose, lumpy texture, so the mashed figure is an upper-leaning estimate. Total ≈ 620 g, ≈ 695 kcal. Hmm, to be more realistic for the visible lumpy mash, I'll keep these values as the best visible-based estimate.
